messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Sev1 - multi-GPU collective failures detected in prod-gpu-pool - routing to #incidents and @oncall
maya: seeing repeated errors in the serving runtime, entire TP3 shards reporting hangs during allreduce
maya: logs show `ncclCommInitRank` timeouts + intermittent `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` around same time
trent: on it, grabbing the latest ksched and pod logs from the hot nodes
maya: paste of tail (from node gpu-pool-12):
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:04Z] ERROR runtime: nccl: timeout after 30000ms (id=0x7fa3)
[2026-03-15T03:12:04Z] ERROR runtime: cuda: driver reset detected on device 0
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] WARN  runtime: communicator closed unexpectedly, rank 1
```
maya: affected cluster id: prod-gpu-pool, model shards using 4-way TP, 2-way PP
dana: are we seeing node flaps or just the communicator level timeouts? can we repro on a single node?
maya: looks like a combination — node 12 had `epoll` disconnects then several pods went into CrashLoopBackOff with `cuda: out of memory` stack traces
ryan: pinging infra: any recent kernel or driver rollouts in that pool? @ops
ops: no planned rollouts in the last 24h. We did move a batch of VMs to a new hypervisor last night but that should be isolated. Checking host dmesg now.
ops: dmesg snippet: "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:17:00: GPU hung and was reset" plus repeated PCIe AER errors on that host
trent: ok, looks hardware-adjacent. Immediate mitigation proposal: drain pods from gpu-pool-12, failover TP ranks to spare nodes, and flip routing to single-GPU fallback variant for the most latency-sensitive routes. Thoughts?
dana: agree. also enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 in the runtime env to avoid whole-communicator hard hangs while we migrate
maya: enabling that now for the canary overlay (will patch jobs in the hot pool). command: `kubectl patch ds runtime-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING","value":"1"}]}]}}}}'`
oncall-bot: manual approval required for live patching to dedicated pools. @trent can you ack?
trent: acked. giving the go for canary patch and node drain. will coordinate with ops to cordon gpu-pool-12.
ops: cordoning node gpu-pool-12 -> `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-12` done. starting graceful drain `kubectl drain gpu-pool-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (evicting pods)
maya: routing change: scaled down TP size for model /large-gen to 1TP x 4DP on the hosted route while we recover. Applied via routing config: `route: /v1/generate -> variant:safe-single-tp`
dana: rolling restart of the runtime pods on the impacted nodes to clear corrupted NCCL communicators. command: `kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-pool-12`
ryan: customer-impact check: CS reports ~18% of requests to the gen endpoint started returning 502s for a 6 minute window at 03:12Z; no data exfiltration or config changes detected. internal alerting linked ticket: INC-3321
customer-success: flagged two enterprise customers, reached out and opened support tickets. told them we're mitigating and will update in 30m.
trent: after canary env var change, can confirm new pods show `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` in env. Observability: per-route error rate down by ~60% for the affected model within 90s of route switch
maya: still seeing a stuck rank in one of the older nodes during drain — manual exec in pod shows `ncclCommAbort` called by rank 2
maya: logs from the stuck pod:
```
2026-03-15T03:14:08Z ERROR runtime: nccl: recv error: communicator lost
2026-03-15T03:14:10Z INFO runtime: attempting graceful shutdown, saving KV cache
2026-03-15T03:14:12Z ERROR runtime: unable to commit KV cache, storage retry
```
maya: stopped the pod (kubectl delete pod) to force reassign. new pod came up on a spare node and joined fine.
trent: ops recommends marking gpu-pool-12 for hardware inspection (PCIe link errors). I'll coordinate with infra to replace the host. For the rest of the pool we should watch for similar AER signs.
ops: added host gpu-pool-12 to maintenance queue INFRA-958, starting replacement workflow
dana: next steps for runtime hardening: add transient retries on communicator init with backoff and fall back to TCP NCCL transport if nvlink fails. create an RFC? I'll draft one.
ryan: for incident timeline + postmortem we'll need approximate scope: affected requests, duration, root cause hypothesis (host PCIe/GPU hang causing NCCL communicator tears), immediate mitigations and longer-term fixes (driver/firmware sweep, NCCL retry logic, route fallback).
maya: quick note: set `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on particularly flaky nodes may avoid certain peer-to-peer hangs while we swap hardware
trent: handing off to night oncall @trent (me) in 10m — I'll own until replacement host is swapped and all TP shards rebalanced. please escalate if error rate creeps up >5% on any model route
sre-robot: scheduled check-ins: 03:30Z verify drain complete, 04:00Z verify rebalanced TP shards, 06:00Z summary report to #incidents
customer-success: will follow up with impacted customers after final confirmation. keeping open tickets flagged high priority
maya: summarizing current status: major node gpu-pool-12 isolated and cordoned, canary env var enabled to avoid hangs, route fallback applied for critical routes, per-route errors reduced but full stabilization pending host replacement. will file incident postmortem once swap is complete.
trent: thanks all — if anyone jumps on make sure to ping me @trent. closing page for immediate action, staying subscribed. :white_check_mark:
